market_says.text: Largest IPO on record — $81.3B raised, topping SpaceX’s $75B.
Opened at $111.50, +34% on the $83 offer price, for a fully diluted value of about $2 trillion at the open.

Index inclusion could bring about $19B of passive buying on the original 825M-share plan; on the final 980M shares the same math implies about $23B — our arithmetic, not the estimate’s.

ANT.what_it_does: Anthropic builds Claude, a family of frontier AI models, and sells it as an API, through cloud partners, and as a subscription (Claude Pro / Team / Enterprise). Revenue is usage-based fees plus subscriptions. The filing says past growth does not predict future growth — and growth is already decelerating sequentially: Q3 revenue rose 47% on Q2, after 144% before (CNBC).

SPCX.what_it_does: SpaceX flies rockets (Falcon, Starship), runs Starlink — 13.6M consumer subscribers — and, since the February 2026 xAI merger, the Super Intelligence segment (Grok, Cursor, AI infrastructure and X). In Q3 2026 the AI segment passed Starlink as the largest revenue line.

NBIS.what_it_does: Nebius is an AI cloud: it builds data centres full of Nvidia GPUs and rents the compute to AI labs, hyperscalers and developers, mostly under multi-year contracts — Microsoft (~$17.4B) and Meta (up to ~$27B) are the named customers. It also runs Avride (self-driving) and TripleTen (edtech); Toloka (data labelling) was deconsolidated in Q2 2025. It holds a stake in ClickHouse. The model is capital-hungry: capacity is funded with debt and customer prepayments, and 2026 capex is guided at ~$27B against ~$3B of revenue. Nebius is the international remainder of Yandex N.V. — the Russian businesses were sold in July 2024 and the company renamed itself the following month. This is not a new IPO: see the listing facts.

market_says.text: Q3 revenue $980.8M (+571% YoY) beat the ~$907M consensus, with adjusted EBITDA of $465.8M — but the shares fell ~16.8% to $128.64 on the guidance cut (2026 revenue to the low end of $3.0–3.4B) and capex raised to ~$27B.

After Q3, Baird cut its target $340 → $200, D.A. Davidson $250 → $125, Truist $355 → $245; Citi cut $265 → $215 but kept its Buy. The Street consensus stays Buy — mean target $234.50 across 22 analysts (S&P Global, via Stock Analysis).

About $325M of Q3 revenue was non-recurring asset-light revenue; without it, the quarter was ~$656M. The $7–9B year-end ARR target was pushed to February, and ARR was dropped as a metric — annualised run-rate revenue was $6.4B at Sep 30.
The shares fell 27% in October alongside CoreWeave as AI-funding fears spread.
Meta agreement of up to ~$27B: $12B of dedicated capacity delivered from early 2027, plus an order of up to $15B under which Meta must buy capacity Nebius cannot sell to others.
